classification.difficultyReason: Infer simple and triple root multiplicities from crossing and flattening, construct the factored equations, and use each y-intercept to determine its scale factor.

content.prompt: Use a similar technique to find the equation of these polynomial graphs.

spec.description: Unshaded equation-driven graph with both ends rising, a simple crossing at −2, a flattened crossing at 4 and y-intercept −16. Ordinary source curve colour is replaced by house black.
spec.mathematics: y=(1/8)(x-4)^3(x+2); roots −2 of multiplicity 1 and 4 of multiplicity 3; y-intercept −16.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph and its intercept labels remain visible; the equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The graph crosses at $x=-2$ and has a triple root at $x=4$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=k(x-4)^3(x+2)\\-16&=k(-4)^3(2)\\-16&=-128k\\k&=\frac18\\y&=\frac18(x-4)^3(x+2)\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unshaded equation-driven graph with both ends rising, flattened crossings at −1 and 1, and central minimum at the y-intercept −2. Ordinary source curve colour is replaced by house black.
spec.mathematics: y=2(x-1)^3(x+1)^3; both roots have multiplicity 3; y-intercept −2.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph and its intercept labels remain visible; the equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The graph has triple roots at $x=-1$ and $x=1$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=k(x-1)^3(x+1)^3\\-2&=k(-1)^3(1)^3\\-2&=-k\\k&=2\\y&=2(x-1)^3(x+1)^3\end{align*}$$
